title: Overnight-Intraday Reversal Everywhere (Market Closure and Short-Term Reversal)
one_line: A cross-sectional strategy buying overnight losers and selling overnight winners for the next day session earned huge gross returns in US stocks (1.68%/day gross, 1993-2014), much weaker in futures including index futures, and it depends on trading right at the open.

findings.statement: CO-OC reversal (overnight losers beat winners intraday): 1.68%/day gross, Sharpe 24 (US stocks).
Holds across futures asset classes including index futures, but much weaker.
Most profit right after the open; a one-minute delay sharply reduces returns.

why.pattern: Liquidity provision: market closure concentrates order imbalances that reverse when trading resumes.
why.mechanism: Overnight price pressure from imbalances reverses once liquidity returns at the open.

reported_results.headline: Overnight-to-intraday reversal everywhere, strongest in stocks.

tradable_edge: Supports overnight_reversal_first_hour_es; the cross-sectional stock version needs stock data we don't have.
angles: Single-instrument version on ES/NQ = existing spec

decay_risk.reason: Gross results; extremely sensitive to execution speed and costs.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
